goal: Determine the smallest useful browser frontend for the working Akashic Records prototype and adapt private CyberAlchemy ontology precedent into a public-safe, Akashic-owned graph profile and implementation direction.
context: Akashic has validated reviewed content, six bounded graph queries, evidence handles, generated Inventory projections, and candidate/review skills, but no browser UI or HTTP API. CyberAlchemy v2 contains private candidate contracts for nodes, relations, default-deny edges, and projections; they are precedent only and cannot become Akashic authority or be copied into public artifacts. Predicted disagreements are explicit: Halford runs human comprehension while Shannon runs semantic preservation on the methodology axis, so a simplification bias in Halford is exposed by lost graph semantics in Shannon; Halford runs progressive disclosure while Ashby runs visible provenance feedback on the methodology axis, so a minimal-screen bias in Halford is exposed by hidden state in Ashby; Shannon owns data and ontology semantics while Ashby owns browser-visible feedback behavior on the methodology axis, so a schema-only bias in Shannon is exposed by non-observable behavior in Ashby; Rittel attacks ownership and precedent while Russell attacks concrete utility and non-vacuity on the attack-vector axis, so a reuse bias in Rittel is exposed by a failed exact witness in Russell. The first frontend must remain understandable to non-programmers while preserving digest, provenance, gap, and claim-ceiling semantics; use exact-binding inside this private working folder, require a reuse/adapt/reject decision for every borrowed pattern, and keep authoring, review persistence, live Git transport, agent execution, authority, publication, and deployment outside the proven scope.
anti_bias_global: human legibility versus contract fidelity versus implementation minimality

agents.angle: Use an empirical task-journey lens over public Akashic content and non-programmer use to minimize cognitive load.
agents.initial_prompt: Study the working Akashic Records repository as a product for people who do not program but know how to work with agents. Derive the smallest primary user journey, information architecture, screen sequence, progressive-disclosure model, terminology, empty/error states, responsive needs, and accessibility risks. Ground every recommendation in current public-safe Akashic content and contracts; do not use private CyberAlchemy vocabulary as user-facing terminology and do not treat the stale README status as current proof. Return exact source paths/selectors and mark observations, inferences, and unverified user assumptions. Budget target: 1800 tokens.

agents.angle: Use a formal contract-trace lens across Akashic runtime schemas and private CyberAlchemy ontology precedent to preserve semantics without importing authority.
agents.initial_prompt: Map the current Akashic feed, generated projection, Q1-Q6, CLI, validation, error, digest, and evidence contracts into a browser-safe frontend adapter. Inspect cyberAlchemy-v2/ontology/README.md, NODE-MODEL.md, RELATION-MODEL.md, and canonical-kinds/ALLOWED-EDGES.yaml only as private candidate precedent. Produce a reuse/adapt/reject table for stable node identity, source references, confidence, challenge/residue, typed endpoints, direction, evidence refs, authority_effect, cardinality, default denial, inverses, cycle policy, and projection separation. Define a public-safe Akashic graph profile with domain-owned node and edge candidates; never make CyberAlchemy a runtime dependency, copy private prose into a proposed public artifact, or treat candidate ontology as canonical. Return exact source paths/selectors inside this private research output and distinguish executed Akashic contracts from architectural inference. Budget target: 2200 tokens.

agents.angle: Use a systems-feedback lens over Akashic provenance state and verified UI Studio browser patterns to make trust boundaries observable.
agents.initial_prompt: Design the frontend state and evidence-feedback model for Akashic. Inspect current provenance, generation, evidence, candidate/review, and read-only boundaries, and examine only verified reusable browser-testing patterns from UI Prototyping Studio such as stable data-od-id targets and Playwright coverage. Identify how users see freshness, evidence, gaps, failures, projection status, and non-authority ceilings without turning the interface into raw JSON. Return exact sources/selectors and do not import private prose or claim human trust from browser evidence. Budget target: 1800 tokens.

Reconcile the three explorer returns into two or three concrete frontend candidates. Each candidate must state its primary user journey, screens, component map, data flow, browser/runtime adapter, technology choice, exact seven-principle and Q1-Q6 witness, accessibility/test approach, cost and complexity, deferred capabilities, evidence ceiling, and public-safe Akashic graph profile. Include a reuse/adapt/reject table for every CyberAlchemy-derived structural pattern and reject any private runtime dependency, copied private vocabulary, or promotion-by-proximity. Produce a candidate picture for the reviewers; do not persist final files. Every load-bearing claim must point to an explorer return and exact source selector. Budget target: 2800 tokens.

agents.angle: Run the precedent gate and test ownership, candidate status, and public/private boundaries for each graph and frontend pattern.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack the synthesized frontend candidates through the precedent gate. Verify actual current owners and comparable patterns in Akashic, private CyberAlchemy ontology, this workspace, and primary external sources where needed. Label candidates build-from-owned, already-deployed, or precedent-clean only after a real search; precedent never kills a candidate. Require every CyberAlchemy-derived idea to remain candidate precedent with a public-safe adaptation or explicit rejection, never a direct dependency or authority import. Return objections and exact repair requests with source selectors. Budget target: 2000 tokens.

agents.angle: Run the non-vacuity gate and require a smallest screen-level witness against exact Akashic nodes, edges, records, and Q1-Q6.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack the synthesized frontend candidates through the non-vacuity gate. For each candidate, construct the smallest screen-level witness using the exact seven-principle feed, proposed Akashic-owned node and edge types, evidence handles, provenance digests, and Q1-Q6 questions. Kill any candidate that cannot demonstrate a concrete useful interaction, typed graph result, distinct failure state, and honest claim ceiling. Return a pass/fail witness matrix and exact repair requests. Budget target: 2000 tokens.

After evidence closure, write findings.md only inside the private working folder. Recommend one smallest frontend direction, preserve viable alternatives and killed candidates, and include the required verdict matrix. Specify the primary journey, screen/component map, browser/runtime adapter, public-safe Akashic graph profile, allowed-edge table, reuse/adapt/reject table, data contracts, technology/testing stack, phased implementation slices, and deferred capabilities. Keep exact private citations in this private findings file, but identify which resulting schema and design statements are safe to restate publicly without private paths or prose. Do not author research.md. Budget target: 3000 tokens.

Audit findings.md only against the dispatch goal. Require a useful answer for non-programmers, exact traceability to current Akashic contracts and selected private precedent, a concrete seven-principle/Q1-Q6 witness, an Akashic-owned graph profile, a complete reuse/adapt/reject table, an explicit read-only adapter boundary, and the verdict matrix. Reject any recommendation that copies private prose or CAV2 identifiers into Akashic, makes private code a runtime dependency, treats candidate ontology as authority, or overclaims live transport, agent execution, deployment, usability, or publication. Recommend accept or return findings.md once to the writer with exact revisions. Budget target: 1900 tokens.
